theater: 芬蘭南部海岸與波的尼亞灣

battle.name: 芬蘭戰爭
battle.theater: 芬蘭南部海岸與波的尼亞灣
battle.brief: 一八〇八年二月二十一日俄軍自阿文科斯基越境攻入芬蘭，瑞典守軍節節退讓，直至十一月簽定奧爾基約基停戰；次年三月俄軍甚至踏冰越過波的尼亞灣攻入瑞典本土，最終瑞典被迫割讓芬蘭。卡面這門一五五〇年的西班牙火繩槍銃早已退場，但它那支單管長槍的身形，仍藏在今日雙方步槍手的火槍與刺刀之中。

kit.name: 火繩槍銃
kit.history: 比步槍輕的長槍。西班牙人帶著它上船，也帶著它進了美洲。

countries:
交戰雙方是俄羅斯帝國與瑞典王國，戰場在今日的芬蘭南部與波的尼亞灣東岸。俄軍方面由皇帝亞歷山大一世御前總攬，名下有布克霍維登、巴拉柯萊·德·托利、卡門斯基、庫爾涅夫、巴格拉季昂、拉耶夫斯基與諾爾寧等將領：一八〇八年二月二十一日，越境的俄軍約二萬四千人分作數縱隊，自阿文科斯基一帶越過邊界，指向洛維薩、漢科、斯瓦爾霍爾姆與斯維埃堡；到一八〇八年八月，進攻芬蘭的俄軍兵力增至五萬五千人，芬蘭戰區的指揮系統先後由布克霍維登、諾爾寧與巴拉柯萊·德·托利三度接掌。

瑞典方面由國王古斯塔夫四世·阿道夫掌軍，芬蘭戰線的最高指揮一八〇八年三月二日由克林斯波爾元帥接任，此外有阿德勒克魯茨、克羅恩斯坦特、桑德爾斯與德貝爾恩分別統率各個兵團；王都斯德哥爾摩卻把最精銳的本土部隊留給南方，留守芬蘭各要塞與城鎮的兵力合計約二萬一千人。這場戰爭自始就卡在兩條戰線中間：一八〇八年三月十四日丹麥－挪威對瑞典宣戰，法國元帥伯納多特在丹麥集結四萬五千人、挪威方向另有三萬六千人，瑞典被迫再抽兩萬三千人守南面與挪威邊際。五月二十六日，英國的遠征艦隊載著穆爾上將所部一萬四千名英軍抵達哥德堡，卻因與國王意見不合始終沒有登陸，只留下十六艘戰列艦與二十艘小艇供瑞典使用；一八〇九年英國海軍索馬雷茲上將再率十艘戰列艦與十七艘小艇進駐芬蘭灣，協助封鎖俄國分艦隊。
countriesEn:
The two belligerents were the Russian Empire and the Kingdom of Sweden, and the battlefield lay in what is now southern Finland and on the eastern shore of the Gulf of Bothnia. On the Russian side the command was held personally by the Emperor Alexander I, with Buxhoeveden, Barclay de Tolly, Kamensky, Kulnev, Bagration, Raevsky and Knorring under him: on 21 February 1808 some 24,000 Russian troops crossed the frontier in a number of columns near Ahvenkoski, driving towards Loviisa, Hanko, Svartholm and Sveaborg; by August 1808 the Russian force in Finland had grown to 55,000 men, and the command of the Finnish theatre passed in turn to Buxhoeveden, Knorring and Barclay de Tolly.

On the Swedish side the war was directed by King Gustav IV Adolf, and the highest command in Finland passed to Field Marshal Klingspor on 2 March 1808, with Adlercreutz, Cronstedt, Sandels and von Döbeln leading separate brigades; Stockholm, however, held back the best troops of the homeland for the south, leaving only about 21,000 men in the Finnish fortresses and towns. The war was from the outset caught between two fronts: Denmark-Norway declared war on Sweden on 14 March, Marshal Bernadotte assembled 45,000 men in Denmark and a further 36,000 faced Norway, and Sweden was forced to detach another 23,000 men to hold the south and the Norwegian border. On 26 May a British expedition carrying 14,000 troops under Sir John Moore entered the port of Gothenburg, but disagreement with the king kept them from ever landing, and only sixteen ships of the line and twenty smaller vessels were left at Sweden's disposal; in 1809 Admiral Saumarez followed with ten ships of the line and seventeen smaller craft into the Gulf of Finland to help blockade the Russian squadron.
people:
芬蘭戰線上最重要的人物是瑞典元帥威廉·莫里茨·克林斯波爾。芬蘭的守備方案本來就以慢戰為宗旨：依計畫先把主力集結在海門一線再徐徐進逼，兵站、糧秣與冬營都按此預設安排。一八〇八年三月二日他才抵達前線，面對已經越境的俄軍，他仍下令全軍退往海門方向，準備在縱深集結後再與俄軍決戰；這一段遲疑讓俄軍在三月裡連下洛維薩、波爾沃、赫爾辛基、漢科與圖爾庫，而他退而不戰的決定，事後被史家視為俄軍得以先行深入的主因之一。其後的瑞典將領各有建樹：阿德勒克魯茨在四月的西卡約基反擊中遏住俄軍前鋒，克羅恩斯坦特於雷沃拉赫蒂推動南進，桑德爾斯率旅在薩伏利亞戰線急行至庫奧皮奧，德貝爾恩在九月十三日朱塔斯取勝後接手北面戰區。

俄軍方面，卡門斯基主張在冬季踏冰跨越波的尼亞灣、兵臨斯德哥爾摩，被諾爾寧視為不切實際而拖延；直到一八〇九年三月，亞歷山大一世派陸軍大臣阿拉克切耶夫赴芬蘭施壓，並親自南下，三月三十一日抵達圖爾庫，撤銷諾爾寧簽下的停戰，改命巴拉柯萊·德·托利為總司令。這位總司令此前已率五千人踏冰自北面越過海灣，三月二十四日進入於默奧；同期巴格拉季昂以一萬七千人攻占奧蘭群島，庫爾涅夫的先鋒更在三月十九日抵達距斯德哥爾摩不足七十公里的瑞典海岸，消息傳回首都才促成停戰談判。

要塞與後方的關鍵人物同樣重要：斯維埃堡守將卡爾·奧洛夫·克羅恩斯坦特以六千人、七百門砲固守海島，最終在五月六日被迫交出整支群島艦隊；斯瓦爾霍爾姆守將格里彭貝里僅有七百人，其中三分之一連可用的武器都沒有。英國方面的穆爾上將率一萬四千人抵達哥德堡而始終沒有上岸，索馬雷茲上將其後率十艘戰列艦進駐芬蘭灣，其部隊在波爾卡拉修築砲台，截斷俄國的海上補給。瑞典國王古斯塔夫四世在戰局崩壞中被指控決策失誤，一八〇九年三月十三日被推翻；卡爾·古斯塔夫·曼納海姆當年以少校身份在芬蘭軍中服役，據其自傳記載，他在戰線上負傷被俄軍俘獲。
peopleEn:
The most important figure on the Finnish front was the Swedish field marshal Wilhelm Mauritz Klingspor. The defence plan for Finland had been built around a war of delay: the main force was to be concentrated on the Häme line and then advance slowly, with depots, supply and winter quarters all arranged on that assumption. Klingspor did not reach the front until 2 March 1808, and faced with a Russian army that had already crossed the frontier he still ordered a withdrawal towards Häme, intending to concentrate in depth and give battle there. That delay let the Russians take Loviisa, Porvoo, Helsinki, Hanko and Turku within March, and his decision to fall back without fighting has been treated by historians as one of the main reasons the Russians were able to advance so deeply. The Swedish commanders who followed each made their own mark: Adlercreutz halted the Russian advance guard in the counter-stroke at Siikajoki in April, Cronstedt drove the advance south at Revolax, Sandels marched his brigade swiftly through Savonia to Kuopio, and von Döbeln, after winning at Jutas on 13 September, took over the northern theatre.

On the Russian side Kamensky proposed marching over the frozen Gulf of Bothnia in winter to bring the war to the gates of Stockholm, and Knorring judged the idea unrealistic and procrastinated; only in March 1809 did Alexander I send the war minister Arakcheyev to Finland to force the pace, arriving himself on 31 March, cancelling the truce Knorring had signed and appointing Barclay de Tolly commander-in-chief. That commander-in-chief had already led five thousand men over the ice to the north, entering Umeå on 24 March; at the same time Bagration occupied the Åland islands with 17,000 men, and Kulnev's vanguard reached the Swedish coast less than seventy kilometres from Stockholm on 19 March, and it was news of that advance that brought the truce negotiations.

The key men in the fortresses and in the rear were equally important: Carl Olof Cronstedt held Sveaborg with 6,000 men and more than 700 guns and was finally compelled to hand over the whole archipelago fleet on 6 May, while Carl Magnus Gripenberg commanded Svartholm with 700 men of whom only a third had serviceable weapons. On the British side Moore reached Gothenburg with 14,000 men and never put them ashore; Saumarez later brought ten ships of the line into the Gulf of Finland, where his men built batteries at Porkkala to cut the Russian sea communications. King Gustav IV Adolf was accused of fatal errors as the situation fell apart and was overthrown on 13 March 1809; Carl Gustaf Mannerheim served as a major in the Finnish army and, according to his own biography, was wounded and taken prisoner by the Russians on the line.
kits:
卡面這件一五五〇年的西班牙火繩槍銃，在一八〇八年的芬蘭戰場上並不出現——它是雙方真正使用的火器的直系祖先：同樣是一支單管長槍，同樣靠一點火星點燃火藥，同樣在滑膛裡打出一團破片，只是在一八〇八年，點火的機構已由火繩換成燧石，槍管旁多了一把刺刀。火繩槍銃的弱點在北極圈邊緣的初春天氣裡格外刺眼：它靠一根浸了硝石的繩索維持火種，一旦受潮或被雪水浸濕便整槍失效，而一八〇八年二月末到三月正是芬蘭南部融雪與春雨交作的季節；它射程短、不配刺刀，也就無法像後來的步槍那樣在散兵線上以刺刀相接決定勝負。

一八〇八年真正扛住整場戰爭的是滑膛燧發步槍配刺刀。俄軍的線列步槍團仍保留著「長矛兵」連的編制，這正是卡面這件火繩槍銃所屬的「槍矛並用」年代的殘餘；瑞典一方的長矛兵則早已在十八世紀中葉裁撤，瑞典營的骨幹只有火槍手與擲彈兵。砲方面，斯維埃堡一個要塞就配置了七百門以上火砲，另有俄軍攻城砲隊與野戰三、六、十二磅砲，以及臼砲與榴彈砲；瑞典在圖爾庫自沉的四十九艘武裝帆炮船雖是船，卻也同時是浮動的砲台。海戰工具同樣退步：瑞典在群島中只有七艘划艇與三十艘武裝帆炮船可用，俄國沿岸分艦隊卻多達近百艘，靠的正是從斯維埃堡繳獲的帆船與從燒毀船上拆下的火砲。

後勤與地形同樣決定裝備的取捨：芬蘭南部多湖沼與森林，春季道路泥濘，車隊只能靠馬匹與人力拖曳；冬季則靠雪橇與滑雪板，軍隊才得以在海門與波赫一線維持冬季宿營；一八〇九年三月跨越結冰的波的尼亞灣，更要求士兵、砲車與糧秣全部改用雪橇輸送。海軍方面，瑞典分艦隊在封鎖期間爆發壞血病，軍官與水手大量病倒，這套裝備與後勤的短板最終比任何一次會戰都更快地決定了戰局。
kitsEn:
The Spanish matchlock arquebus of 1550 on the card face did not appear on the field of battle in Finland in 1808: it is the direct ancestor of the weapons the two sides actually used. Both are single-barrelled long guns, both are fired by a spark igniting the charge, both throw a cloud of fragments down a smooth bore; by 1808 only the ignition had changed, from a match cord to a flint, and a bayonet had been added to the barrel. The weakness of the matchlock was particularly sharp in the early spring of a country on the edge of the Arctic: the weapon depended on a cord soaked in saltpetre, and once that cord was damp or soaked with meltwater the whole gun was dead, and late February to March 1808 was precisely the season of thawing snow and spring rain in southern Finland. Its short range and its lack of a bayonet also meant it could not decide an engagement by the bayonet in the skirmish line as the later musket could.

What actually carried the war was the flintlock smoothbore musket with bayonet. The Russian line infantry regiments still contained companies of pikemen, the surviving remnant of the age of pike and shot to which the arquebus on the card belongs, whereas the Swedish pike troops had been abolished in the middle of the eighteenth century and the Swedish battalion rested on musketeers and grenadiers alone. On the artillery side, the single fortress of Sveaborg mounted more than 700 guns, and there were in addition the Russian siege train, field guns of three, six and twelve pounds, and mortars and howitzers; the forty-nine armed sloops the Swedes burned at Turku were ships, but they were floating gun platforms at the same time. The naval hardware had equally declined: Sweden could field only seven galleys and thirty armed sloops in the archipelago against nearly a hundred Russian coastal vessels, an advantage built directly on the sailing craft and the guns stripped from burned ships captured at Sveaborg.

Logistics and terrain determined the choice of equipment as much as the fighting did. Southern Finland is a country of lakes and forest, and in spring the roads turned to mud, so wagon trains could move only on horse and muscle; in winter it was sledges and skis that allowed the armies to keep their winter quarters on the Häme and Pori line; and the crossing of the frozen Gulf of Bothnia in March 1809 required men, guns and provisions all to be moved on sledges. On the naval side the Swedish squadron suffered outbreaks of scurvy while maintaining the blockade, officers and sailors falling ill in large numbers, and this weakness of equipment and supply decided the war faster than any pitched battle.
tactics:
俄軍的戰術核心是一條沿海岸推進的縱隊與一組封鎖堡壘的算計。二月二十一日的越境並非一次強攻，而是數縱隊同時南下：先取洛維薩、圍斯瓦爾霍爾姆，再於二十四日奪波爾沃、二日入赫爾辛基、十六日下庫奧皮奧、二十一日佔漢科與圖爾庫。奪取海岸線本身就是戰術目標：俄軍知道只要把海岸攥在手裡，英國與瑞典的登陸部隊就無從著陸，瑞典守軍只能退入內陸，在一條被拉長的縱深防線上被逐段吃掉；斯維埃堡五月六日開城後，繳來的群島艦隊更讓俄國在狹窄的群島水道中取得主動。

瑞典一方的守勢戰術則建立在兩個念頭上：一是依計畫在海門一線集結主力再徐徐反攻，二是把帶不走的東西統統毀掉。克林斯波爾三月二日接手後仍令全軍退往海門聚兵；三月裡圖爾庫港內近五十艘武裝帆炮船與大批糧秣被一併自沉或焚毀，免得落入俄軍之手。這一退一守換來了時間：四月十八日西卡約基，阿德勒克魯茨以縱隊反擊擊潰俄軍前鋒；四月二十七日雷沃拉赫蒂，克羅恩斯坦特又勝一場，瑞典一度奪回主動。但春季融雪令道路泥濘，瑞典的推進屢屢因「爛路」停頓，兵力雖在推進，速度卻起不來。

北面與東面則是另一套打法。桑德爾斯的旅在薩伏利亞急行深入，逼迫俄軍將領圖奇科夫在沿途每一座要塞都留駐分隊，自己手上只剩四千人馬；芬蘭各地的游擊隊隨即在東部興起，一直打到舊芬蘭的哈米納一帶，使俄軍在縱深處不得不分兵應付。秋季形勢逆轉：卡門斯基以一萬一千人的軍團在九月一日奪庫奧爾塔內、二日取薩爾米、十四日在奧拉瓦伊斯取得全戰役最重要的勝利，瑞典的攻勢由此收斂。十一月十九日奧爾基約基停戰，瑞典軍隊被逐出芬蘭鄉土。

冬天俄軍又把戰術推到前所未有的一步：踏冰穿越波的尼亞灣，一支取道奧蘭群島直趨斯德哥爾摩方向，一支自北面進入於默奧，一支繞道托爾尼奧。三月的長距離冰上行軍之後，四月以來戰線又拉回芬蘭南部。海上，瑞典曾企圖封鎖漢克半島阻止俄國分艦隊北上，卻因西德斯特倫指揮失當而被解職；瑞典的答案是以接連的小規模登陸反擊：六月十九日萊穆、二十五日瓦薩、七月三日克里斯蒂納斯塔德與卡斯基寧、八月一日吉倫貝格爾率一千名志願兵、九月十七日帕爾瓦松、二十六日海爾辛基村一連串登陸，屢屢得手又屢屢被迫撤回。登陸多由裝備不良、訓練不足的部隊執行，加上瑞典海軍未能封死漢克外海的航路，這一整套海岸騷擾始終無法改變大陸戰線的勝負。
tacticsEn:
The core of Russian tactics was an advance along the coast combined with the isolation of the fortresses. The crossing of 21 February was not a single assault but a number of columns moving south at once: Loviisa was taken and Svartholm invested, then Porvoo fell on the 24th, Helsinki on 2 March, Kuopio on the 16th, and Hanko and Turku on the 21st. Seizing the coastline was itself the tactical object, for the Russians understood that once the shore was in their hands no British or Swedish landing could make good a footing, and the Swedish defenders would be driven inland and eaten up segment by segment along a stretched line of depth; when Sveaborg opened on 6 May, the captured archipelago fleet gave Russia the initiative in the narrow channels of the archipelago as well.

Swedish defensive tactics rested on two ideas: to concentrate the main force on the Häme line according to plan and then counter-attack slowly, and to destroy everything that could not be carried away. Klingspor, taking over on 2 March, still ordered the army back towards Häme to concentrate; in March the nearly fifty armed sloops in the roads of Turku and large stores of provisions were sunk or burned rather than fall into Russian hands. That retreat and that holding bought time: on 18 April at Siikajoki Adlercreutz counter-attacked in column and broke the Russian advance guard, and on 27 April Cronstedt won again at Revolax, and for a moment Sweden had the initiative. But the spring thaw turned the roads to mud, the Swedish advance was repeatedly halted by impassable roads, and although men were pushed forward the pace could not be got up.

In the north and the east a different pattern was used. Sandels's brigade marched deep through Savonia, forcing the Russian commander Tuchkov to leave detachments in every fort along his route and reducing him to four thousand men; partisan fighting then rose across the Finnish countryside, reaching as far east as Hamina in Old Finland and forcing the Russians to spread their strength in depth. In the autumn the tide turned: Kamensky with a corps of 11,000 won at Kuortane on 1 September, at Salmi on the 2nd, and at Oravais on the 14th in the most important victory of the whole campaign, and the Swedish offensive contracted. On 19 November the Convention of Olkijoki was signed and the Swedish army was driven out of the Finnish countryside.

In winter the Russians took tactics a step further than before: marching over the frozen Gulf of Bothnia, one column by way of the Åland islands towards Stockholm, one to the north into Umeå and one round by Tornio. After the long ice marches of March the line was drawn back into southern Finland from April onwards. At sea the Swedes tried to blockade the Hanko peninsula to keep the Russian coastal squadron from moving north, and lost Cederström's command over it; the Swedish answer was a series of small landings: Lemu on 19 June, Vaasa on the 25th, Kristinestad and Kaskinen on 3 July, a thousand volunteers under Gyllenbögel on 1 August, Palva Sund on 17 September and the Helsinki village landing on the 26th, each landing successful and each withdrawal forced. The landings were carried out by troops poorly equipped and poorly trained, and the Swedish navy failed to seal the sea route past Hanko, so that the whole series of coastal raids could never change the result on the mainland.
data:
可核對的數字大致如下。一八〇八年二月二十一日，越境的俄軍約二萬四千人，分作數縱隊自阿文科斯基一帶進入芬蘭；同日洛維薩失守，斯瓦爾霍爾姆被圍。留守芬蘭各要塞與城鎮的瑞典軍合計約二萬一千人。波爾沃於二月二十四日、赫爾辛基於三月二日、庫奧皮奧於三月十六日、漢科與圖爾庫於三月二十一日相繼失守；圖爾庫港內近五十艘武裝帆炮船被焚毀。斯瓦爾霍爾姆守軍七百人，其中僅約三分之一有可用武器，全堡火砲多無砲車，圍城歷時約一個月，至三月十八日開城，期間守軍僅一人受傷。斯維埃堡守軍六千人，配置七百門以上火砲，糧秣儲備足以支撐至一八〇八年夏天，經長期談判後於五月六日投降，瑞典群島艦隊幾乎完整落入俄軍之手。五月，英軍上岸部隊與地方民兵在奧蘭的庫姆林厄作戰，守軍在兩小時的戰鬥後投降。

兵力對比方面，一八〇八年八月進攻芬蘭的俄軍為五萬五千人，瑞典方面估計三萬六千人；卡門斯基指揮的軍團為一萬一千人。芬蘭境內的英國遠征軍一萬四千人於五月二十六日抵達哥德堡，留下十六艘戰列艦與二十艘小艇；一八〇九年索馬雷茲率十艘戰列艦與十七艘小艇進駐芬蘭灣，在波爾卡拉修築砲台，俘獲俄船三十五艘、焚燒二十艘，於九月二十八日離開波羅的海。

具體戰鬥的數字：六月十九日韋格薩克以二千六百人於萊穆登陸，次日被圖爾庫方向三千餘名俄軍逼退；六月二十五日貝根斯特羅勒以一千一百人於瓦薩附近登陸，攻入城中後被約三千名俄軍迫退；七月二十一日與八月二日，瑞典炮艇在塔爾霍爾門與桑德奧斯特倫與俄軍分艦隊交手。九月一日卡門斯基部奪庫奧爾塔內，九月二日取薩爾米，九月十三日德貝爾恩於朱塔斯取勝，九月十四日俄軍在奧拉瓦伊斯取勝。九月二十六日多爾戈魯科夫與圖奇科夫會師，桑德爾斯退卻；二十九日布克霍維登簽署停戰，亞歷山大一世拒絕批准，十二月以諾爾寧接替。一八〇九年三月十七日巴格拉季昂以一萬七千人占領奧蘭群島，十九日庫爾涅夫的先鋒逼近至距斯德哥爾摩七十公里內，二十四日巴拉柯萊·德·托利率五千人進入於默奧，二十五日托爾尼奧守軍投降。

傷亡方面，估計俄軍死傷約一萬人，瑞典軍死傷約七千人，另有約五萬三千人死於疾病與其他非戰鬥原因。
dataEn:
The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. On 21 February 1808 some 24,000 Russian troops crossed the frontier in several columns near Ahvenkoski; Loviisa was taken the same day and Svartholm was invested. The Swedish troops left in the Finnish fortresses and towns came to about 21,000 men. Porvoo fell on 24 February, Helsinki on 2 March, Kuopio on 16 March, and Hanko and Turku on 21 March; the nearly fifty armed sloops in the roads of Turku were burned. The garrison of Svartholm numbered 700 men, of whom only about a third had serviceable weapons, and most of the fortress guns had no carriages; the siege lasted about a month and the fortress opened on 18 March, with only one man wounded in action. Sveaborg held 6,000 men with more than 700 guns and stores sufficient to last until the summer of 1808; after prolonged negotiations it surrendered on 6 May, and the Swedish archipelago fleet passed almost intact into Russian hands. In May the British landing force and the local militia fought at Kumlinge in Åland, and after a two-hour battle the garrison surrendered.

On the comparison of strength, the Russian force in Finland in August 1808 was 55,000 men against an estimated 36,000 for Sweden, and the corps commanded by Kamensky numbered 11,000. The British expedition of 14,000 reached Gothenburg on 26 May, leaving sixteen ships of the line and twenty smaller vessels; in 1809 Saumarez brought ten ships of the line and seventeen smaller craft into the Gulf of Finland, built batteries at Porkkala, captured thirty-five Russian vessels and burned twenty, and left the Baltic on 28 September.

The figures of particular engagements: on 19 June von Vegesack landed 2,600 men at Lemu and was forced back the next day by more than 3,000 Russians from the direction of Turku; on 25 June Bergenstråhle landed 1,100 men near Vaasa, entered the town, and was driven out by about 3,000 Russians; on 21 July and 2 August Swedish gunboats engaged the Russian coastal squadron at Tallholmen and Sandöström. On 1 September Kamensky's men took Kuortane, on the 2nd Salmi, on 13 September von Döbeln won at Jutas, and on the 14th the Russians won at Oravais. On 26 September Dolgorukov joined Tuchkov and Sandels fell back; on the 29th Buxhoeveden signed an armistice, Alexander I refused to ratify it, and in December Knorring replaced him. On 17 March 1809 Bagration occupied the Åland islands with 17,000 men, on the 19th Kulnev's vanguard came within seventy kilometres of Stockholm, on the 24th Barclay de Tolly entered Umeå with 5,000 men, and on the 25th the Swedish garrison at Tornio capitulated.

On losses, the Russian dead and wounded are estimated at about 10,000 and the Swedish at about 7,000, with a further 53,000 dying of disease and other non-battle causes.
cause:
這場戰爭的直接起因，是拿破崙的體系把瑞典推到了一條沒有出口的路上。一八〇七年提爾西特和約之後，俄皇亞歷山大一世在九月二十四日致信瑞典國王古斯塔夫四世，聲稱兩國的和平關係取決於瑞典同意遵守和約中對英國貿易的限制，實質上就是要求瑞典加入大陸封鎖體系。英國則害怕瑞典倒向法國，於是在二月八日先與瑞典結盟，並以皇家海軍封鎖波羅的海。海軍實力本已吃緊的瑞典不可能同時對抗英俄兩面，卻也無法拒絕：拒俄則與英國的聯盟與封鎖立即破裂，拒英則等於把波羅的海拱手讓給法國。

第二層原因是瑞典自身的戰略兩難。一八〇八年三月十四日丹麥－挪威宣戰，北方邊境與南面海岸同時告急，瑞典必須把最精銳的本土部隊留給南方，把芬蘭當成可以放棄的遠東前哨；同時國王把希望寄託在英軍登陸斯堪的納維亞、一舉反攻丹麥與挪威的計畫上，最精銳的師團因此沒有投入芬蘭，留在芬蘭的只有約二萬一千人。戰爭的計畫本身也早已過時：芬蘭的守備方案未計入武器進步、部隊機動力的提高與新修道路的價值，許多要塞尚未完工，已完工者又多半年久失修，連最強的斯維埃堡都缺少全部面向陸路的防禦工事。

第三層是後勤與準備的失誤。國王擔心囤積軍需會被俄國視為挑釁，芬蘭方面並未儲備足夠的糧秣與彈藥；宣戰本身也延到四月才正式完成，讓俄軍得以先行越境而不受條約拘束。這一連串決策最終把瑞典推到兩難：向俄開戰就要在沒有補給體系、沒有足夠兵力的芬蘭土地上打一場守土戰，而打到冬季又必然面對俄軍在冰封海灣上的奇襲。
causeEn:
The direct cause of the war was that Napoleon's system pushed Sweden onto a road with no exit. After the Treaty of Tilsit of 1807 the Russian Emperor Alexander I wrote to King Gustav IV Adolf of Sweden on 24 September, stating that the peaceful relations between the two countries depended on Sweden's agreement to abide by the limitations of the treaty on trade with Britain, which in practice meant joining the Continental System. Britain, afraid that Sweden would fall towards France, allied itself with Sweden first, on 8 February, and the Royal Navy blockaded the Baltic. A Sweden whose sea power was already strained could not fight against Russia and Britain at once, yet it could not refuse: to refuse Russia meant the immediate break of the British alliance and the blockade, and to refuse Britain meant handing the Baltic over to France.

The second layer of cause was Sweden's own strategic dilemma. Denmark-Norway declared war on 14 March 1808, the northern border and the southern coast were both threatened at once, and Sweden had to keep the best of the homeland troops in the south and treat Finland as a distant eastern outpost that might be sacrificed; at the same time the king built his hopes on a British landing in Scandinavia and a counter-stroke against Denmark and Norway, so the finest regiments were not sent to Finland and only about 21,000 men were left there. The war plan itself was out of date: the defence plan for Finland took no account of the advance in weaponry, of the mobility of the troops or of the newly improved roads, many of the fortresses were unfinished, those that were complete had mostly fallen into neglect, and even the strongest of them, Sveaborg, was missing all of the land-side defences designed to hold against a besieger.

The third layer was failure of preparation and supply. The king feared that large stocks of military supplies would be read by Russia as a provocation, and no adequate stocks of food and ammunition were laid in in Finland; the declaration of war itself was delayed until April, which allowed the Russians to cross the frontier first without being bound by any treaty. Together these decisions left Sweden in a vice: to fight Russia meant fighting a defensive battle in a theatre with neither a supply system nor enough troops, and to see the winter out meant facing a Russian stroke across the frozen gulf.
impact:
第一層影響落在北歐的地緣格局上。芬蘭的割讓使瑞典王國失去約三分之一的人口與土地，東界由波的尼亞灣退到亞爾的內海與波的尼亞灣西岸；俄國隨後在割讓地上建立芬蘭大公國，保留古斯塔夫時期的1772年憲法直到1919年，並於1812年把十八世紀取得的舊芬蘭併入，芬蘭從此成為俄國帝國裡一個有自治憲法的成員。奧蘭群島的歸屬在條約中懸而未決，此後成為俄國與瑞典之間反覆出現的爭端，一八五四年奧蘭戰爭後更被列為不得武裝的中立地帶。

第二層是瑞典本國的變革。一八〇九年三月十三日的政變推翻古斯塔夫四世，卡爾十三世即位，隔日制憲會議通過一八〇九年憲法，瑞典由專制王權轉入新王統治時期；一八一八年貝納多特王朝以《王位繼承法》確立，開啟了長達半個多世紀的拿破崙式君主制在瑞典的實踐。學者的研究還指出，芬蘭的失陷使瑞典精英感受到東方的存亡之威，官僚體系的腐敗與低效成為必須清理的對象，行政改革由此推動。

第三層是北歐的整體戰略與英國的介入。瑞典在條約後被迫加入大陸封鎖體系並對英國船隻關閉港口，隨即在1810年與英國正式開戰；一八一〇年一月六日在俄國斡旋下與法國訂立巴黎條約，北歐才從拿破崙體系的戰場中暫時抽身。英國海軍在波羅的海的存在，既支援了瑞典，也同時把瑞典綁在反法同盟的一邊。

第四層在軍事與制度上：一場以小部隊登陸、群島遊擊與遊擊隊騷擾為主要形態的戰爭，說明在沒有縱深可以展開會戰的地方，分散、機動與海運補給比正面決戰更決定成敗；芬蘭士兵的傷亡數字與歸還問題，同時暴露了遠征軍在後勤與醫療上的脆弱，迫使瑞典在戰後重整常備軍與徵兵制度，也促使北歐國家真正建立聯邦式的互助經驗。
impactEn:
The first layer of impact fell on the geography of the north. The loss of Finland took away roughly a third of the Swedish realm's people and land and pushed the eastern frontier back onto the Gulf of Bothnia and the Åland Sea; Russia then created the Grand Duchy of Finland on the ceded territory, retained the Gustavian Constitution of 1772 there until 1919, and in 1812 annexed Old Finland, so that Finland became a member of the Russian Empire with an autonomous constitution of its own. The status of the Åland islands was left unsettled in the treaty and became a recurring dispute between Russia and Sweden, and after the Åland War of 1854 the islands were declared a demilitarised zone.

The second layer was the transformation of Sweden itself. The coup of 13 March 1809 overthrew Gustav IV Adolf, Charles XIII was elected king, a constitution was passed by the assembly the following day, and Sweden moved from absolute monarchy into a new kind of royal government; in 1818 the Act of Succession established the Bernadotte dynasty, opening more than half a century of Napoleonic monarchy in Sweden. Studies by political scientists have argued that the loss of Finland made the Swedish elite feel an existential threat in the east, and the corruption and inefficiency of the Swedish bureaucracy became something that had to be cleaned up, so that administrative reform was driven forward.

The third layer was the strategy of the north as a whole and the British intervention. By the treaty Sweden was forced into the Continental System and closed its harbours to British ships, and in 1810 it formally went to war with Britain; the Treaty of Paris of 6 January 1810, mediated by Russia, brought Sweden out of the Napoleonic theatre for the time being. The presence of the Royal Navy in the Baltic supported Sweden, but at the same time tied Sweden to the anti-French coalition.

The fourth layer was military and institutional. A war fought mainly in small landings, archipelago skirmishes and partisan operations showed that in places where there was no depth in which a pitched battle could be fought, dispersal, mobility and sea-borne supply decided the outcome more than a frontal engagement. The casualty figures and the repatriation of Finnish soldiers exposed the fragility of an expeditionary army in matters of supply and medical care, pushing Sweden after the war to reform its standing army and conscription system, and giving the Nordic countries their first real experience of acting together.
result:
一八〇九年九月十七日，瑞典與俄國在芬蘭的腓特里克斯哈姆簽訂和約：瑞典割讓整個芬蘭以及托爾訥河以東的全部屬地，奧蘭群島的主權懸而未決；瑞典並承諾加入大陸封鎖體系、對英國船隻關閉港口，隨即在1810年與英國正式開戰。純從戰場看，瑞典是這場戰爭的敗方：芬蘭全境在一八〇八年十一月之前已落入俄軍之手，瑞典軍隊被逐出芬蘭鄉土，十一月十九日簽訂的奧爾基約基停戰只不過是承認既成事實；一八〇九年三月俄軍踏冰越過波的尼亞灣，一度逼近斯德哥爾摩，迫使瑞典接受城下之盟的談判。

會戰層面的關鍵是九月十四日奧拉瓦伊斯一役：卡門斯基以一萬一千人的軍團在此擊敗瑞典方面，扭轉了此前德貝爾恩在朱塔斯取得的局部勝利，北線局勢就此定型。北方戰線則由古斯塔夫·瓦赫邁斯特在八月的反擊收場，薩瓦爾、拉坦與皮特奧幾戰互有勝負，最後一場皮特奧之戰以俄軍勝利告終。九月二十八日英國海軍撤出波羅的海，此後瑞典再無外力介入的餘地。

戰爭的結束並不等於問題的解決。芬蘭的割讓使瑞典王國大為縮小，但也迫使它在隨後數十年重建國防：國防財政與徵兵制度重整，軍隊的常備化與後備制度逐步成形，國王與議會之間的權力關係也因一八〇九年的憲法而重新排列。對俄國而言，這場戰爭解決了彼得大帝以來未竟的西北邊界問題，維堡與整個芬蘭海岸線從此成為帝國的內部防線，北歐的均勢則被徹底改寫：瑞典從北歐的強國降為一個仍保有本土而失去東翼的次一等國，北歐此後的政治，只能在瑞典與俄國這條新邊界上重新安排。
resultEn:
On 17 September 1809 Sweden and Russia concluded the Treaty of Fredrikshamn: Sweden ceded the whole of Finland and all her possessions east of the Torne river, the sovereignty of the Åland islands was left unsettled, and Sweden undertook to join the Continental System and to close her harbours to British ships, which was followed by a formal declaration of war on Britain in 1810. Purely on the field the Swedes were the losers: the whole of Finland was in Russian hands before the end of November 1808, the Swedish army was driven out of the Finnish countryside, and the Convention of Olkijoki of 19 November was nothing more than the acceptance of a fait accompli; in March 1809 the Russians crossed the frozen Gulf of Bothnia, came close to Stockholm and forced Sweden into negotiations at the walls of its own capital.

The decisive engagement was Oravais on 14 September: there Kamensky with a corps of 11,000 defeated the Swedish, reversing the local success that von Döbeln had won at Jutas and fixing the situation on the northern front. The northern line was closed out by Gustav Wachtmeister's counter-offensive in August, the actions at Sävar, Ratan and Piteå going one way and the other, and the last of them, the battle of Piteå, ending in a Russian victory. On 28 September the Royal Navy left the Baltic, and from then on Sweden had no outside help left to draw on.

The end of the war was not the end of the problem. The loss of Finland reduced the Swedish realm drastically, but it also forced the country to rebuild its defence over the following decades: the defence finances and the conscription system were reorganised, the standing army and the reserve system were gradually reformed, and the balance of power between king and diet was reset by the constitution of 1809. For Russia the campaign settled the unfinished question of the north-western frontier left over from Peter the Great, and Vyborg and the whole Finnish coastline became the empire's internal defence line, while the balance of power in the north was completely rewritten: Sweden went from being a great power of the north to a second-rank state that still kept its homeland but had lost its eastern wing, and the politics of the north had henceforth to be rearranged along the new frontier between Sweden and Russia.
